pages.title: German historical school
pages.extract:
This is an article about a school of thought in the area of law. For economics, see historical school of economics.

The German historical school of jurisprudence is a 19th-century intellectual movement in the study of German law. With Romanticism as its background, it conceived of law as the organic expression of a national consciousness (Volksgeist). It stood in opposition to an earlier movement called Vernunftrecht ('rational law').

pages.title: Ja'fari school
pages.extract:
The Jaʿfarī school, also known as the Jafarite school, Jaʿfarī fiqh (Arabic: الفقه الجعفري) or Ja'fari jurisprudence, is a prominent school of jurisprudence (fiqh) within Twelver and Ismaili (including Nizari) Shia Islam, named after the sixth Imam, Ja'far al-Sadiq. In Iran, Jaʽfari jurisprudence is enshrined in the constitution, shaping various aspects of governance, legislation, and judiciary in the country. In Lebanon, this school of jurisprudence is also accounted for in the legal system of the country and Shia Muslims can call upon it for their legal disputes. During the French Mandate in Lebanon and after independence, Jaʿfarī jurisprudence became institutionalized through Jaʿfarī courts, where legal practice reflected not only religious doctrine but also citizenship, gender, and state authority. It was on January 27, 1926 when the Ja'fari school was formally recognised by the Lebanese state, after the recognition of the Shi'a community as independent and leading to the approval of Ja'fari personal status law. Consequently, Ja'fari courts became established across Lebanon, with courts of first instance in regional centres, and a central appellate court located in Beirut. While Ja'fari jurisprudence was initially established in relation to Lebanese citizens as it was recognised by this state, its use across state borders became popular as many followers of the Ja'fari madhhab claimed adherence to the court. During the Mandate Period, foreign Ja'fari individuals appealed to these courts with the hope of overturning rulings from alternative courts in nearby countries. 
It differs from the predominant madhhabs of Sunni jurisprudence in its reliance on ijtihad, as well as on matters of inheritance, religious taxes, commerce, personal status, and the allowing of temporary marriage or mut'ah. Since 1959, Jaʿfari jurisprudence has been afforded the status of "fifth school" along with the four Sunni schools by Azhar University. In addition, it is one of the eight recognized madhhabs listed in the Amman Message of 2004 by King Abdullah II of Jordan, and since endorsed by Sadiq al-Mahdi, former Prime Minister of Sudan. Historically, Ja'fari and Sunni Hanafi courts were alternatively and strategically appealed to, depending on the jurisprudence that would favour the litigants' claims in regards to issues of personal status law. This was particularly done by women, for instance, in divorce cases, for which Ja'fari courts required stricter conditions.

pages.title: Historical school (disambiguation)
pages.extract:
Historical school are movements in the study of the methods used by historians.

Historical school of political economy, a movement in late political economy
